ranked.headline: Frozen protein and chemical embeddings scored against campaign-grouped, structure-aware benchmarks
ranked.summary: Enzyme kinetics, stability and binding-site predictors built on frozen PLM/CLM features are now judged by campaign-split benchmarks and experimental validation.

ranked.headline: Generative models predict perturbation responses and infer dynamics from single-cell snapshots
ranked.summary: Flow matching, disentangled VAEs and language-linked foundation models now target unseen perturbations, while OT and physics priors recover dynamics from snapshots.

ranked.headline: Generators conditioned on explicit constraints are judged by exposure, synthesis, and assembly rules
ranked.summary: New conditioning schemes span pharmacophores, pockets, conjugate components and single-residue edits, while PBPK re-scoring changes which generated candidates rank well.

ranked.headline: Cell-type networks and donor-aware models tie molecular programs to disease outcomes
ranked.summary: TriSCOPE, SPIN and network-guided plasma proteomics apply cell-type and network-level models to population cohorts for disease attribution and prediction.

ranked.headline: Omics databases move evidence to CpG, cell-type, spatial-niche and mutation resolution
ranked.summary: A batch of NAR database updates, plus canine and lung tumor atlases, refine where molecular evidence is anchored: CpGs, cell types, niches, kinase mutations.

ranked.headline: Structure-linked annotation databases add curated content and machine-actionable, agent-ready access
ranked.summary: Six database updates pair expanded structural and literature-derived annotation with versioned APIs, MCP servers and workflows for programmatic use.

ranked.headline: Evaluations probe whether protein models encode physical structure or dataset-specific regularities
ranked.summary: New probes show protein language model and foundation model performance depends on invariances, patterning rules and dataset composition rather than learned structure.

ranked.headline: Curated datasets, target selection and modular pipelines support structure-based ligand modeling
ranked.summary: New datasets, pocket-based target selection and an open screening pipeline address the input and workflow needs of structure-based ligand modeling.

ranked.headline: Transcript-level resources and tools resolve polyadenylation and isoform usage across scales
ranked.summary: Preprints and a database paper pair isoform and poly(A) resolution with single-cell tools, aging atlases, structural modeling and proteomics.

ranked.headline: Generative ensemble models and physics-based energetics replace single static structures
ranked.summary: Preprints extend ensemble generation to proteins, antibodies, IDPs and RNA while published work quantifies pocket dynamics, ligand strain and protonation shifts.

ranked.headline: Learned and decomposition methods mine microbial genomes and metagenomes for functional and mobile gene content
ranked.summary: New resources and methods catalogue resistance enzymes, mobile elements, prophages and pangenome modules across microbial genomes and metagenomes.

ranked.headline: Public sequence archives and metadata layers are being harmonized for reuse and re-analysis
ranked.summary: New tools harmonize GEO metadata and automate microbiome re-analysis while NCBI updates its sequence resources, easing reuse of public sequencing data.

ranked.headline: Predicted and designed structures are being judged against membrane, energetic and ensemble criteria
ranked.summary: New studies test AlphaFold outputs and design models against bilayer geometry, beta-sheet organization and local frustration, with GPU tooling enabling proteome-scale analysis.

ranked.headline: Spatial and single-cell methods define gene-, relationship- and neighborhood-level units of inference
ranked.summary: New spatial methods test morphology-expression links, gene relationship shifts and neighborhoods, alongside a 12.6M-cell atlas for disease-wide comparison.

ranked.headline: Bias correction, survival pseudo-observations and harmonized reanalysis refine association inference
ranked.summary: Selection-bias methods, pseudo-observation outcomes and uniform meta-analysis sharpen how genetic and omics associations are estimated across species.

ranked.headline: Benchmarks test whether perturbation and drug-response predictions rest on concordant data and informative priors
ranked.summary: New benchmarks show limited cross-source drug-response concordance and prior-dependent predictability, challenging how perturbation models are trained and evaluated.

ranked.headline: Significance tests and explicit error models are being added to transcriptomic partitioning and prediction
ranked.summary: New tests attach null models to spatial domains and scRNA-seq clusters, while audits expose where predictions and sequencing depth fall short.

ranked.headline: Audits test what model scores can certify in CRISPR, siRNA and protein sequence design
ranked.summary: New preprints test whether design-model outputs and confidence scores can support claims, finding public CRISPR cohorts and pLM confidence readouts fall short.

ranked.headline: Count-based, uncertainty-aware and sequence models refine variant effects on expression and chromatin
ranked.summary: New preprints and papers pair personalised or count-based expression models with sequence predictors to score noncoding variants across cell types.

ranked.headline: Coding and repeat content defined from cross-genome alignment, orthology and family evidence
ranked.summary: New tools derive repeat, coding and protein-family catalogs from assemblies, alignments and orthogroups without relying on a single reference annotation.

ranked.headline: Comparative genomics links shark epigenomes, Wnt gene repertoires and intron evolution
ranked.summary: Chromosome-scale shark genomes, genome-wide intron surveys and 1,961-vertebrate Wnt analyses now enable structural evolution inference at scale.

ranked.headline: Genomic language models are being benchmarked for viral and pathogen sequence embeddings
ranked.summary: Pretrained genomic language models are being extended to raw nanopore signals and pathogen-scale embedding tasks in recent preprints and publications.

ranked.headline: Computational pipelines assign function to hypothetical bacterial and phage proteins
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend functional coverage of hypothetical bacterial and phage proteins beyond Pfam and ECOD-based annotation.

ranked.headline: Sequence-based deep learning advances protein, DNA, and epitope prediction
ranked.summary: Language-model pretraining, structure-aware graphs, and reinforcement learning are being applied across DNA, protein, and immunology tasks.

ranked.headline: Curated multi-species databases map circRNA translation, RBP sites and snoRNA targets
ranked.summary: Expanded cross-species resources now link circRNA translation evidence, RBP target sites and snoRNA annotation across model organisms.

ranked.headline: Computational antibody and binder design assessed beyond raw predicted binding
ranked.summary: Recent work extends computational binder design to multi-variant antigen targets, agentic workflows, and binding trade-off diagnostics.

ranked.headline: Pairing limited cancer measurements with external references or a second modality
ranked.summary: Foundation-model features, external atlases, and multimodal fusion now enable inference of missing molecular, clinical, and cell-state information from incomplete cancer data.

ranked.headline: LLM-driven extraction of chemical-effect evidence from toxicology literature
ranked.summary: Corpus-scale LLM pipelines now convert toxicology full texts into structured chemical-effect evidence, with human-AI review in one design.

ranked.headline: Single-cell multiomic atlases map regulatory programs across basal ganglia and brain
ranked.summary: Joint single-cell profiling of chromatin and transcriptomes now spans primate, mouse and human basal ganglia at million-nucleus scale.

ranked.headline: Alignment-free and sketch-based tools reduce cost of viral and sequence inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and a publication report tools that avoid full alignment or exhaustive comparison to scale viral and protein sequence analysis.

ranked.headline: Sequence and signal models for RNA therapeutic design and RNA measurement
ranked.summary: Deep learning and benchmarking methods now target RNA design and measurement directly from sequence, raw current, and mass spectra.

ranked.headline: Curated peptide databases and ML tools for ADMET and antimicrobial activity prediction
ranked.summary: Peptide therapeutics are expanding, yet poor permeability and in vivo stability still decide which candidates reach the clinic.

ranked.headline: Segmentation-free and noise-corrected methods resolve cell-state and spatial sources
ranked.summary: Recent preprints address ambient RNA, doublets, batch effects and segmentation to attribute single-cell and spatial measurements to underlying sources.

ranked.headline: Stricter evaluation and heterogeneity-aware models in biomedical ML prediction
ranked.summary: Shifted-split evaluation is exposing where biomedical ML generalization claims need explicit, auditable support.

ranked.headline: Pretraining inputs and readout design reshape compact biomolecular model performance
ranked.summary: Benchmarks now show global metrics can overstate gains, so compact models are being judged on region-aware and delta-level readouts.

ranked.headline: Compressed indexes for k-mer dictionaries and pangenome exact-match search
ranked.summary: Recent preprints extend SBWT colored indexes and move-structure matching to terabase-scale assemblies and compact k-mer dictionaries.

ranked.headline: Reimplemented analysis pipelines speed up genomic, CRISPR screen and CLIP-seq workflows
ranked.summary: Recent preprints and papers port established sequencing and CRISPR screen analyses to faster, reproducible open tools.

ranked.headline: Computational models are being re-engineered for cross-scale biological inference
ranked.summary: Recent preprints test how simulator, network, and generative model choices shape inference across epithelial, cancer, and genomic scales.

ranked.headline: Proteomics searches reach proteoforms and dark proteome; peptide coverage gaps measured
ranked.summary: Expanding what proteomics searches can assign now comes with explicit measurement of which peptides and proteoforms are actually covered.

ranked.headline: Explicit models of unobserved processes refine rate and lineage inference in genomics
ranked.summary: Simulation-based inference and likelihood methods now estimate local rates and lineage structure directly from genomic data.
